kooli.name: Kooli
kooli.headline: Kooli: site attendance and weekly payroll for civil contractors, verified by photo.
kooli.lede: Built for contractors juggling day labourers across multiple sites. Supervisors log attendance with a photo, and payroll adds itself up correctly every week.
audience: Civil and construction contractors running more than one site
Site supervisors recording daily labour attendance
Owners who pay workers weekly

features.title: Photo-verified attendance
features.body: Supervisors log attendance and work hours with a photo, so the record is backed by evidence.

features.title: Multi-project payroll
features.body: Weekly worker payroll is calculated across all your projects instead of being reconciled by hand.

features.title: Works offline on-site
features.body: Supervisors can keep recording attendance where the signal is poor, and it syncs when they are back online.

features.title: Installs like an app
features.body: Kooli is a web app that installs on a phone's home screen, so there is nothing to download from a store.

faq.question: Does it work without internet on site?
faq.answer: Yes. The supervisor flow is built offline-first, so attendance can be recorded without a connection.

faq.question: Who is it for?
faq.answer: Civil contractors who track day labourers across sites and pay them weekly.

club-management.name: Club Management
club-management.headline: Club management software for Lions Clubs and member-run organisations.
club-management.lede: Membership, dues, and events, sorted. Built for Lions Clubs, sports clubs, and other member-run bodies juggling subscriptions, treasurers, and events across spreadsheets and group chats.
audience: Lions Clubs and other service clubs
Sports clubs and associations
Treasurers and secretaries who chase dues by hand

features.title: Members and dues
features.body: Keep a member register, set subscription plans, record payments, issue receipts, and see outstanding dues and defaulters at a glance.

features.title: UPI payments and reminders
features.body: Members can pay by UPI, and the treasurer can send payment reminders instead of chasing people individually.

features.title: Projects, expenses, and finance reports
features.body: Track projects and expenses, print project reports, and export the annual finance report for your CA.

features.title: Events, RSVPs, and notices
features.body: Invite members to events, capture RSVPs and attendance, and send notices with push notifications.

features.title: Role-based access
features.body: Officers and staff see what their role needs, and each club gets its own branding.

faq.question: Is it only for Lions Clubs?
faq.answer: It is built around Lions Clubs, and it also suits sports clubs and other member-run organisations.

faq.question: Can we import our existing members?
faq.answer: Yes. Members can be imported instead of typed in one by one.

faq.question: Can members pay dues online?
faq.answer: Yes, by UPI, with receipts recorded against their account.

audience: Tuition centres and coaching classes
Teachers running several batches
Centres that want parents kept informed every week

features.title: Batch-wise attendance
features.body: Mark attendance for each batch and grade in one place.

features.title: Test scores and remarks
features.body: Record test scores and teacher remarks against each student.

features.title: Weekly parent reports
features.body: Parents get a weekly summary of attendance and progress, without teachers writing each one by hand.

faq.question: Can we run several batches?
faq.answer: Yes. Attendance is tracked batch by batch, across grades.

faq.question: What do parents receive?
faq.answer: A weekly summary of their child's attendance, scores and remarks.

gold-scheme.name: Gold Savings Scheme
gold-scheme.headline: Gold savings scheme software for jewellery shops: run 11+1 schemes without the paper register.
gold-scheme.lede: Run monthly gold savings schemes for your jewellery shop: 11 + 1, 12 + bonus, flexible pay-as-you-wish, or gold-weight accumulation. Record every payment with a receipt, let customers follow their savings on their phone, and settle each account with a signed statement.
audience: Jewellery shop owners running monthly savings schemes
Counter and field staff who collect instalments
Customers who want to see their savings on their phone

features.title: Design any scheme
features.body: Start from presets like 11 + 1, 12 + 7% bonus, 10 + 2, or flexible gold weight, then adjust bonus, due day, grace days, late rules, and early-closure rules. A preview shows what a customer ends up with.

features.title: Daily gold rate with a typo guard
features.body: The owner enters the 24K, 22K and 18K rates each morning. A rate far from the last one asks for confirmation, and once a payment has used a rate it is locked so a customer's grams never change.

features.title: Receipts and payments
features.body: Record cash, card, UPI or bank payments and print numbered receipts. A wrong entry can be cancelled with a reason and stays on file marked cancelled.

features.title: UPI approvals
features.body: Customers pay from their passbook and enter the UTR number. Staff check it against the bank and approve or reject with a reason the customer can see.

features.title: Customer passbook on their phone
features.body: Customers see their own savings, pay by UPI, and get reminders, so fewer people ask at the counter.

features.title: Settlement statement at maturity
features.body: The app works out the bonus, waivers and the jewellery value or grams, shows every figure first, and prints a statement for the customer to sign.

features.title: Overdue tracking and reports
features.body: See late, overdue and lapse-due accounts, follow up with the defaulters report, and export reports to CSV.

steps.title: Enter today's rate
steps.body: The owner sets the gold rate for each purity every morning.

steps.title: Design the scheme once
steps.body: For example a Swarna 11 + 1 scheme, with its bonus and late rules.

steps.title: Enrol customers
steps.body: Each account gets a number like GS-0001 and a month-by-month schedule, with the scheme's terms locked in for that customer.

steps.title: Collect every month
steps.body: Customers pay at the counter, to a field collector, or by UPI, and every payment gets a receipt.

steps.title: Settle at maturity
steps.body: The owner reviews the bonus and jewellery value, confirms, and prints the statement to sign.

faq.question: Which scheme types are supported?
faq.answer: 11 + 1, 12 + bonus, 10 + 2, flexible pay-as-you-wish schemes, and gold-weight accumulation, where each payment becomes grams at that day's rate.

faq.question: Can we move from a paper register?
faq.answer: Yes. Set a start date in the past, up to about a year, and record the earlier payments with the dates they were paid.

faq.question: Who sets up our shop?
faq.answer: KashV creates the shop and the owner's login. The owner then creates staff logins, and owner or staff create customer logins.

faq.question: Do you store customers' Aadhaar or PAN numbers?
faq.answer: No. For ID proof you record the type and only the last 4 digits.

tournament-management.name: Tournament Management
tournament-management.headline: Tournament management software for badminton and pickleball: run the whole event from your phone.
tournament-management.lede: From registration to winners. Players register and pay by UPI from one shareable link, you make a fair draw in seconds, referees score on their phones, and every team gets a "You're up!" alert when it's their turn. Better fixtures, faster scores, happier players.

screens.alt: Tournament page showing the entry fee, closing time and a Register your team button
screens.caption: Register & pay

screens.alt: Public fixtures page with semi finals and finals for each category
screens.caption: Live fixtures

screens.alt: Referee scoring screen with a plus one button for each team
screens.caption: Score from the court

screens.alt: Winner poster card listing winner, runner and semi finalists with prize money
screens.caption: Winner poster

audience: Clubs, academies and associations organising tournaments
Organisers who want matches to start on time
Referees and scorers keeping score on a phone
Players who want to know their court and time without chasing anyone

features.title: Registration and UPI payments
features.body: Players register their team and pay the entry fee by UPI from one shareable link. A repeated UTR number is blocked, and you approve each payment in one tap or mark it paid in cash.

features.title: Fewer entry mistakes
features.body: The app warns you about odd or shared mobile numbers and players already in another team in the same category. Tick off age proof as players show it.

features.title: Fair draws and fixtures
features.body: Teams are drawn at random with byes added automatically, for as many categories as you run. Already made the draw elsewhere? Enter those fixtures yourself instead. Players follow the public fixtures page.

features.title: Match queue and courts board
features.body: Give matches a queue number and a court, and see every court at a glance: what is in play, the live score, who is refereeing, or free. A warning stops one player being sent to two courts at once.

features.title: Live scoring from any phone
features.body: Each referee gets a private link and scores with a tap per point, with undo and a manual correction. Many courts run in parallel, as single set or best of 3.

features.title: "You're up!" alerts
features.body: Teams get a notification when their match is called, the next two matches get "You're up soon", and with auto-announce the next match is called as soon as a court frees up.

features.title: Reports, winners and your own app
features.body: Download entries, results and payouts as CSV or PDF, and share on WhatsApp. Closing the event publishes the winners page and poster cards. Every tournament is its own installable phone app with your name and logo.

story.heading: Built by a player who was tired of waiting.
paragraphs: Sport has always been a big part of our founder's life. He is a regular on the tournament circuit and a frequent winner.
But the same frustrations kept showing up: tournaments running late and no organised way of running the day. Players were left waiting around when they should have been playing.

So he built the tournament app he wished every organiser had: registration and payments, a fair draw, live scores on every court and an alert when it's your turn. The day runs clean, and it runs on time.

steps.title: Set up the tournament
steps.body: Name, date, fee, UPI ID, categories, prizes and logo are all set inside the app, and the tournament gets its own phone app.

steps.title: Share one link
steps.body: Players register their team and pay by UPI from the same link.

steps.title: Approve and draw
steps.body: Check each payment, close registration, then make the draw for every category.

steps.title: Run the day
steps.body: Queue the matches and call them to courts. Referees score on their phones and teams get alerts.

steps.title: Close and announce winners
steps.body: One tap locks the results, publishes the winners page and poster cards, and congratulates every placed team.

sports.name: Badminton
sports.detail: single set to 30 or 21, or best of 3 sets to 21

sports.name: Pickleball
sports.detail: games to 11, 15 or 21 (win by 2), or best of 3 games

faq.question: Which sports does it support?
faq.answer: Badminton and pickleball. You pick the sport for each tournament and the scoring format for early rounds and for semi finals and finals.

faq.question: Do players have to install anything?
faq.answer: No. They open your tournament link on their phone to register, pay and follow fixtures. They can add it to their home screen and turn on alerts to get "You're up!" notifications.

faq.question: How do I know a player has really paid?
faq.answer: The player pays by UPI and enters the UTR number. You check it against your bank or UPI app, then approve it or reject it with a reason the player can see. The same UTR can't be used twice.

faq.question: Can we use a draw we already made?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter your fixtures yourself instead of using the app's draw, with byes where you need them.

faq.question: Can one account run several tournaments?
faq.answer: Yes. Each tournament has its own name, logo, fee and UPI ID, with up to three organisers who can manage only their own tournament.
